notes: Router said no-platform. el-armandos.shop is a .shop TLD but does NOT redirect (curl -sIL returns 200 directly, cloudflare-hosted, not a farm) and carries real content - the restaurant's own site, matching the playbook's 'does not redirect and carries real prices' exception. The own site's /menu page is data-quality-poor: it lists 100 dish <h3> titles across 13 named sections (Soft Tacos, Tuesday, Combinations, Monday, Wednesday, Enchiladas, Tortas, Tacos Hard Shell, Breakfast Burrito, Side Orders, Extras, Kid's Meals, Others) but only 27 of those 100 have a non-empty <span class="dish--price"> next to them in the static HTML - the rest render the same item ids elsewhere on the page with an EMPTY price span, so those categories (Soft Tacos, Combinations, Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday daily specials, Enchiladas, Tortas, Tacos Hard Shell, Breakfast Burrito, Side Orders, Extras, Kid's Meals) show item NAMES with NO price anywhere reachable by curl - likely populated by client-side JS this fetch cannot see. All 27 priced pairs happen to sit under the h2 header literally labeled 'Others' in document order; kept that label since relabeling them into a guessed category would be inventing structure the page doesn't confirm. Dropped one outlier, 'Two Chicken Tacos' at $1.50 (the same combo-plate section otherwise runs $10.50-$14.35 and rolled-taco items run $3.90-$5.35 - a $1.50 full order does not fit either band and reads as a broken/glitched price render, not a real menu price) - not recorded. Price level for the remaining 25 items is plausible for a 2026 Poway taco shop (combo plates $13.50-$14.35, burrito fillings $6.50-$10.75, rolled tacos $3.90-$5.35). This is a PARTIAL capture: combo plates, burrito-filling choices and rolled tacos are priced; standalone tacos, enchiladas, tortas, breakfast burritos, side orders, extras and kid's meals are all present by name on the site but have no reachable price and were not recorded.
